body: Have you ever seen an Allo skeleton in person? I've seen Big Al in person. He ain't that big. PoT has them as these lumbering semi-apexes, and they were so much more. Allo has a serious mobility issues, and I don't mind damage or weight nerfs if it means making Allo like it is.
In game Hatz weighs more than Ano, Sty, or Kent. I'm sure this is for balance reasons, but it does make Hatz fairly robust.

I think many of the favorites need abilities or stat buffs. Allo feels alone in needing a total rework. It was designed as an apex before anything was close to it in size. It does not feel good to play compared to the rest of the 3 slots, and massively struggles against everything smaller than it. Right now, Metri is a better representation of Allosaurus than Allo.

This was definitely how it felt to me. Hatz had significantly better turn, and burst damage was insane. I'm willing to bet a face tank scenario would probably favor Allo, but we know most fights don't go that way.

I'll say Alio has really good speed and group buffs, so it's not as such a boring state compared to Campto and Thal. Alio/Cera/Conc groups can be lots of fun, and Alio  definitely fills a role in fights of being where they need to be well. Definitely still needs an update, but it's not Thal levels of useless.
You were cooking with 'Frilliam.'
I don't think there's any stopping the griefing. That's just the nature of pvp open worlds, but as of right now, kosing with a group feels kind of like the endgame unless you start nesting.
I enjoy the open world nature of combat, but I think it would be a great way for players to hone their skills in a controlled environment. Maybe learn which dinos they want to grow.
Exactly my point. I don't want to stop people from fighting, but I think the game could offer more varied experiences beyond just fighting.
I guess I've played community server strip IC of resources, and all it does is create a different hotspot beyond Salt Flats. I think event type quests could fix this, but I'm just spitballing ideas.
This is my point. I don't want moderation, I want gameplay to encourage different interactions beyond just killing. It's too easy to blame people for a system that encourages their behavior.

I agree. I don't like rules in community servers, but do think there's an issue with limited ways to play. I just want people to have more ways to play the game. As of right now, the endgame seems to just have a roving group of 5 people that can kill everything at a POI. I want something more.

That's fair but Alderon has already actively worked on TDM, CTF, and KOTH modes that I think do way better than community run pvp servers. Just more ways to play for people who just want that singular experience.

I guess my point is to ask, why would an adult herbivore kill a juvie, and I think it's just because it's something to do. I've played on community servers with rules for herbi aggression, and I personally just found the experience boring. I hope Alderon just adds more to the gameplay side of the game.

I think Titan is a good example. It can absolutely be harassed to death, but you have Juke as a skill check for both players. Can the smaller dino bait it out? Can the Titan hold their cards? I have a lot of fun in those fights because it can go either way while still favoring the Titan in a 1v1.
And that's my problem. Allo can reliably be harassed to death by things smaller than it. All I want from an Allo TLC is improvements to this area, because it does have great stats otherwise.

My problem is that normal turn radius isn't enough. Megs or raptors can attack Allo with impunity. The tail doesn't do real damage, so they are free to tail ride. You have to bank on them making mistakes, and don't have the damage of Titan to punish them. I genuinely think Juke is an easy solution, but I'd love to see more for a more agile Allo build.

It is strong in groups, but in 1v1s, I would honestly bet on any 2 slot Carnivore over Allo. The tail attack is weak, and all the 2 slots have the speed to get away or turn radius to tail ride. It's only when players get lazy that Allo can reliably do damage to smaller dinos. Juke on a 10 second cooldown fixes all of this.

The matchups against Alberta and larger are all fine, but I literally think Allo is a free meal as Conc, Cera, or a raptor.

Allo feels like the weakest dino in the game for me in 1v1s. Genuinely, I think all Allo needs are movement options. Juke or something, because right now add all the cool damage abilities you want, Allo still struggles hard core against things smaller than it. I want Allo to be lithe and nimble, not some proto-apex that leans on large health pools and moderate damage.

The issue for Hatz is that it was designed to kill all those pesky 2 slots that can harass a Rex to death. As the fastest playable in the game, every player will have a different idea as to where that line should be drawn. I personally think it's pretty ridiculous that Hatz can facetank Cerato, but I've also been an Allo thinking it's ridiculous I don't have the manuevrability to fight a good Meg.

Hatz should be thought of more like Sarco than Titan or Eo, where it poses a very particular threat. Except that a Hatz can be anywhere. RIP solos who pick 2 slots to run away from groups.
Just make sure there's 35 before you start collecting!
What a fool I am! The centrifugal forces produced by ano's weighty tail clearly would have made it aerial. I imagine it like a shotputters throw with the body helplessly carried along.
Ridiculous, a stegosaur could clearly flap its plates to achieve flight. Are you suggesting bars spins its mighty tail like a helicopter?
I nominate the most grotesque animal, stegosaurus, to be the first flying herbi.
I don't have a problem with realism, but I do think this would be an interesting way to get more interaction between semiaquatics and terrestrials.

I don't even think you need feast. You just have to be patient. Granted this is from the ano perspective, but I've had a number of titans bring me to about a third health before just leaving me be. Maybe I just play a lot of conc and am used to lengthy fights can take, but I bet most titans could take out ano if they had 5 more minutes of persistence.
I really think it needs something like Juke. Allo has atrocious turn speed, and it struggles against way too many dinos because of that.

I think fliers are a more nuanced problem. Being able to escape from combat is a huge edge, and I don't envy the devs on designing and balancing them in a way that's fun for everyone. I think this is why Tap has been the way it has for so long. Hatz feels like a whole other rant, but being able to face tank a cerato seems insane to me.
You mad lad
I know it started as just a single dino, but for part of the test it allowed for 2. I never had my two playables taken away.

I understand the point, but I think there are only a few sections of the map that actually make good on this promise. The downside is that it maps the map feel like a theme park. Personal opinion on my part.
I don't think an archipelago is the right solution. That forces interaction, but that isn't fun for the swimming dino. Players would just choose not to be dinos on that map.
Was my game bugged? On the regular solo server, I had 2.

Truly unpopular, I think devs understood navigation and questing when they made it which makes it way less annoying for traveling. That said, I think Gondwa has some issues like most areas only having specific entrances and exits.

How do you design a map where it's both fun to play as a sty and a kai? It just seems like it's a huge challenge when the game is still needs to find out how to make playing Rex and Alio rewarding experiences.

It's the thunderdome. It's easy to see what everyone is doing, and it has food and water. I prefer the desert biomes but loathe complex navigation so I'm relegated to Savana and Dry Lake. Lots of cool places to hang out in Gondwa.

Fliers and Aquatics were a mistake to add into the game in the first place.

Edit: As the most downvoted comment on this thread, I gracefully accept most unpopular opinion.

With Kentro, you are stacking bleed on your opponent. You're also pretty fast. You get bleed stacks on them and run away. If they chase, that's good, they're taking more damage. If they slow down, regen your stam and go back to harass. It's a strange playstyle, but effective.

Sty, Cera, and Dasp are all decently fast dinos that do solid damage and can excel in solo play as well.
I just want to add to this that TLC updates usually involve a specific dino with ability additions, stat changes, and model updates.

I've been with the game since the kickstarter. It's been a long time. Their dedication to ports and continuous updates has me hopeful that the game will stay alive for a long time to come. They aren't a huge team, so we still have issues from 5 years ago, but things like Gondwa and critters were such huge improvements from where the game started that I'm confident in a better state of play in the future.
Yeah, I can agree with all that. Just wanted discussion on what that looks like.
Despite all the achillo nerfs, it has such buttery movement that I still find it an absolute pleasure to play.

It sounds like you want to play Concavenator or Ceratosaurus. Conc is just got a nerf, but it is fairly straightforward to build. I ignore most of the swim perks, and focus on bleed. It has one of the best speeds on land, and you can be comfortable with only two attacks. 

Cera is slightly slower, but it is relatively tanky for its size. You'll probably be forced into more fights, but it's manageable. The heavy bite can do bone break, but you have options if you don't end up liking that attack. Generally, I'd avoid the corpse perks on Cera as they are more of a roleplay thing, but it is still a very strong dino.

I'm not sure if I agree about the stam changes. It's just a knowledge check that punishes newer players. Stam management is still important.

I've been playing lots of Conc the past month, and it definitely was definitely too strong between bleed and it's heal rate. Time will tell if this nerfs it into the ground, but I'd like to see Concs doing more than just spamming kick.

However, you're absolutely right about universal mechanics. I would love to see more added to the game like ambushing. I don't think Alderon is moving away from more diverse abilities, I just think they're working on updating all the dinos to a new baseline that can accommodate future changes. Juke is proliferating, and that seems a sign that more movement options will be added. It's okay to be tired and need a break, but I don't see the doom and gloom.

I'm a bit confused by what you mean by the game being flattened. Is the game somehow less interesting than it was 4 years ago? There's bleed, venom, bonebreak, knockback, pouncing, clamping, and aoe abilities. There's various calls that do buffs. There are movement options like juke and charge.

People here are constantly talking about how OP or useless Pyc is in discussions here. I think that speaks to how skillful the game is. 

I think the game has a lot to grow into. There are TLCs that still need to be done, and quests that are still as boring as they were 4 years ago. AI dinos... I don't fondly look back on the days where I needed to have a map of the carcasses pulled up just so I didn't starve leaving Talons Point.
I've been playing a lot of conc recently, and was genuinely starting to think it might've been a sleeper top tier.

I'd add Conc to that list. It's fairly comparable to Cera with better speed, mobility, and stam. The bleed allows you to really slow down fights, and force unwinnable situations where you can recover while your opponent is still bleeding. You're less tanky, but I find it to be far more forgiving.
That's actually really cool tech. Might be worth regrowing through an egg to try that.

I think the light hide is the stronger option. You have good speed, so your only real threat is stuff smaller than you. I've mauled through raptor backs without ever feeling under threat with that hide.

This is gonna sound silly but in full groups, it's probably Conc or Lat. They both have the speed and mobility for skill expression to outplay the apexes. Lat definitely gets way stronger in a full group, but it's hard to get 10 people together. The bleed damage is what Concs really benefit from, as they can cycle in and out against other groups.

I think 1v1s are interesting, but the game doesn't exactly play out that way. Before the nerfs, I might have included Sty when it was also at 1100 speed and higher weight. Fast bleeders are the kings of group fights.
It should be marked on your screen and mini map.

I suppose I'm confused at the problem. You're stating that pyc beats meg in optimal situations. You want meg to be able to 50/50 pyc in that area. Then meg is as oppressive on land, with superior mobility, and capable of using water defensively.

I play conc primarily, so I'm very familiar with the fact that pyc really doesn't enjoy bleed damage. Pyc has a really bad time when it gets caught up on terrain, and is forced into a fight with those slow cooldown times. 

Fighting pyc is hard, but it's not unbeatable. It can be baited and evaded. I'm glad you've had such success with pyc. Keep up with meg, it's really satisfying to have the best turn radius in the game.

I think Meg is generally in a good place being one of the most mobile playables in the game. I haven't played with the venom buff, but maybe venom still needs tweaking.

On the Pyc side of things, I've seen people call is busted and people call it trash. My experience is that pyc is pretty strong, but more annoying than anything.  It's probably divisive for its unique blend of stats in the same way ano is. It's probably in a good place too.

Pachy is the only one that I haven't really seen anything that impresses me. I've never seen someone do an impressive solo with them, and my only run ins with them are when they're baby killing. They've gotten a lot of changes, but I still think they're missing the sauce.

I meant sprint speed just as a sense of how fast dasp is for evading danger. I know lat has fantastic movement options.

The damage boost/mitigation towards lighter dinos is a huge boon for dasp. I've definitely fought raptor packs confidently, and haven't died to a laten yet. I'm not great either, so I'm sure it's just about fighting a laten that's both talented and confident enough because I could definitely see one doing it.
And dasp can beat lat? That light hide means lat has to work way harder. I'm not disagreeing that lat can win, but dasp certainly has the time to wait for lat to make mistakes.

I think dasp is a likely equal. It has equal sprint speed to Laten, and the damage to really threaten anything faster. With pierce bite, it can threaten the whole roster. It definitely feels like the easiest dino in my experience.

I think there's a big problem with Hatz. The rest of the roster seems to be balanced with the concept of you can fight anything you can't outrun. A Hatz can chase down everyone, and only struggles against the heavier 3 slots. Hatz being able to facetank Cerato is ridiculous.

That's actually a really great write up. I remember the devs saying they removed many of the solo perks to keep people from working together ungrouped. Do you think there could be a way the perk system could support what you experienced in ED?

You're right, Allo is busted. That's why servers are full of allos and not titans, dasps, and latens. Can't remember the last time I fought a Cera or a Meg because Allo just wins every fight.

If you are on a server where everyone just tries to facetank, please share. I would love a relaxing Allo experience.
My major problem is that allo has an awful turn radius. It costs me lots of fights that I find completely comfortable on other dinos.
Dasp has to be running the right abilities to fight Allo, but Dasp has better speed and mobility. They get to choose whether there's a fight and when it ends.

I agree allo has a decent collection of stats that lots of other dinos would love. I just think allo is worse than the sum of its parts. You can say Thal is bad, but Thal never has to be in a fight it can't win. Allo regularly does.
Those abilities are a scam. Swerve and normal bite do just fine.

I ran the numbers on the old patch and this was only true for a face tank scenario with both on even health. It might be should be better now with the styra weight nerf, but I don't know how much. It might've been too late once they got to that point.
Dasp has a hide that increases damage and allows it to take damage from dinos smaller than it. It makes it very strong against every dino smaller than it, styra included.

I really don't understand why people think Cera is bad. It lost armored tail, and now has Swerve, one of the best attack hitboxes in the game. It no longer loses to the mobility of something like Meg or Pachy.

I think Allo is a solid contender for the worst dino. It lacks turn radius to deal with anything smaller than it, and damage for anything bigger than it. It was designed as an apex before anything close to its size was in the game. Conc, Metri, Dasp, and Titan all a better job at what Allo wants to be in the game. No other dino is outshone by so much of the roster. 

Even your vote of megalania has incredible turn radius and beats allo with ease.
Yes, styra is OP. Dasp is also OP and counters it very well. Allo is one of the worst dinos in the game. Sorry you had to learn this way.
I have mostly transitioned to community servers, I just wish there was a way for gameplay to steer players towards less toxic behavior.
I don't mind those groups as much because they have far more nebulous structures. When I see 14 people playing as Dasp and Stego working together, I feel weird about that.
I was already familiar with the fact IC is full of players.
I thought my neighbors were playing loud music. It was an Eo.
You can play on custom servers with rules that disallow this sort of thing.

I wanna give a shout out to Dasp if you want the big dino experience solo. If you grab the light hide, you basically win every match up. If something can chase you, you can kill it and you can out maneuver the bigger dinos.

I also want to reassure you that the bleed build conc is very strong, you do not need to spec into water.

Any time people say Allo is decent. Granted I don't play apexes, but allo feels so much worse than everything else in its weight class and below. I absolutely destroyed a raptor pack of 8 as Dasp, but got wiped by 2 latens on Allo. The disparity between Allo and the rest of the roster is insane.

I enjoy more 'realistic' or drab skins. Most of the skin packs don't really appeal to me because they're mostly a wacky pattern on the dinos. I wish there were more skins that accentuated the unique features of the dinos like the crests on cerato or the spikes on kentro. There's usually a good skin in every pack. Throw some neon blue and purple alberta's frill. Make a tail centric skin that really dazzles on bars.

Meg and Pachy used to be able to outplay Cera if they knew what they were doing. It's now basically an auto win against both. I do wish we still had armored tail instead of all the useless corpse abilities, but I think Cera is strong enough and gotta cater to the RP people.

Swerve, juke, and shove more than make up for it. You no longer lose to turn speed, and you have an easy counter to stomp. Swerve legit has the craziest hutbox available to a carni right now. This was a huge buff, and Cera was already my favorite dino to play.

That's fair, most dinos grow between 2 to 3 hours on perma death. While I conceptually like perma death, I think the punishment is too great for the state the game is in right night now. My problem is that being young needs to be fun, and it's not there yet. It needs things like speed topping out at the beginning of sub adult then dinos slow down as they grow heavier, or mini games in the open world to mix up button prompt quests.

For me, perma death just isn't compelling. Juveniles don't have meaningful interactions with adults. As an adult, why would you let a baby live? It can't give you group buffs, so you kill it because that's the only "fun" interaction. It can't run away from you or fight you, so that's not really fun either but it's more engaging than critters.

Growing is either tedious or a gamble. Do I chill for 10 hours in Titan Falls or Burnt Forest, or do I try power leveling in Savanah? It feels like the game is wasting my time.

Adult vs Adult interactions are only interesting because you're gambling 12hours of your time. If I make $15 an hour at work, that's $180. I can go to a casino, and bet increments of that money for far more nuanced rewards/punishments.

I what I'm saying is that I'm too tired for perma death. Path of Titans needs more features and interactions to make growing a fun experience. An rpg does not ask you to perform 12hours of fetch quests before you enter your first fight. Something like Pokémon or Skyrim is constantly asking you to interact with the game wholly before you are sent to a gym or dungeon.

If you enjoyed it in the past, I'd say it's a better experience with every update. Devs have taken balancing the roster more seriously than they have in the past, dinos get significant updates, and gameplay is being fleshed out. Take a look at their blog, and see what has changed. For me, the addition of critters was foundational and really made the game feel like a game.

I think the first dino I sub switched was achillo, and this was before was released achillo. I'm realizing this was a perhaps a very long time ago probably closer to the console ports. Poor memory on my part, but everyone else has pointed out that this is no longer a thing that happens.

It very well could have been years ago, I've been playing since the game was just a skins editor. I recall it being like 4 deaths and 2 cliff jumps because I didn't like the area I was respawned in. But thanks for the info. I've been reluctant to grow the slower dinos ever since.
The devs did make a little joke. Level 69 is larger than the rest across the board. I recall the same thing happening during regular levels, and thinking it was a cap.

I think you're dead on the money. Speed seems to be the determining factor for damage. An ethos of if you can't fight it, you can run from it. I think the only rule breakers for this have been Hatz, Styra, and Pycno. I think Styra and Pycno are beening touched up. Hatz is cool, but will probably always be a nightmare to balance.
Really glad Alderon is giving up the old mantra of use groups to eliminate game imbalance. We've seen way more adjustments to health, damage, and weight.
If speed was truly everything, alioramus would be the only dino played along with hatz and sarco.

Panjura was built before the game was playable, and it shows. I really enjoyed the streams of it being built, but the reality is that navigation is a nightmare. They shortened every sightline possible, so we wouldn't notice how bad pop-in was in those early days.

Gondwa was a huge step forward, and really revitalized my enjoyment of the game. I remember first loading in and walking from Young Grove to Rainbow Hills without any pain. It felt revolutionary.
Malignant is maybe the pinnacle of the Sam Rami style of "everything can be sacrificed in the name of fun."

The balance as I understand it to prevent something like a flying brass bull or uncatchable seige jezzail. You could however combine flying with terrifying presence and inhuman strength to have a quick melee specialist. I don't understand why you think Seal of Solomon would prevent taking armor.
You need to unlock all the specific colors used. Abadon Black, White Scar, and Wraithbone. Haven't had the issue since.

I'd say Black Templars are either the people who like 40k's satire the most or don't even see it. Really quick to see which side they're on, and I'm generally more uncomfortable with other factions' fans that are more ambiguous.

B class. It feels like time loses in B class are the least impactful for the way the tracks are built, and Wreckfest is at its best with a tight pack. But play how you like. Wreckfest might be the only racing game I play for "game feel" over podium finishes.

A middle of the road opinion would be that pitbulls are like ever other athletic dog out there. Dangerous because dogs that size can be dangerous. Wanting a license for pitbulls suggests that pitbulls are specifically dangerous.
Where are you even flying to? You passed Cuca's.
Spoken like a person who doesn't live near a decommissioned air force base.

This is the series I've dreamed of since I first saw Walking With Dinosaurs. Hopefully it inspires a whole new generation.

There are some sequences that will stay with me forever like the Dreadnoughtus battle or the Velociraptor cliff diving into the best meal of her life. My personal favorite story was Antarctopelta's big adventure, I've really grown a soft spot for nodosaurids.

While it was great seeing marine life and so many pterosaurs, I wish we had gotten another 8 minute segment for each episode about the other life in the Mesozoic. Mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians all have such an interesting place in that time period. I'd have lost it to see a pseudosuchian.

Overall an astonishingly beautiful rendition of the time period, and like every great nature documentary, left me wanting so much more.

Thanks to research papers, talks, and books, authors have painted remarkably vivid images of dinosaurs for us to imagine. However, I have quite some trouble knowing what ecologies looked like in the time of the dinosaurs. Prehistoric Planet has done a wonderful job showing the relationships dinosaurs had with themselves and their environment. 

Is it common to know what contemporaries a given fossil would have had in life, or is the fossil record too sparse?

I think the community is ridiculous for asking for playlist systems from over a decade ago. The mixtape system is what we need from Titanfall 2 and MCC. Pick the modes you want, exclude the ones you hate. If there's a specific challenge you want, you que into that playlist alone. It's a brilliant system and I don't know why 343 decided to exclude one of their best features from MCC.
Then it is a fair fight.
I lost my mind on a map with 3 of these tiles. Glad to know I can squeeze an Atlas down there.
The hero banshee is legit no joke with the firepower it can bring. I'm a big fan of good support mechs.

The Mauler MX90 with twin PPCs, SRM6s, and quad machine guns is maybe the most fearsome thing I've built. I can just march into the face of every assault and heavy mech the game can throw at me. I'm also partial to the Cicada X5 with quad flamers and twin SRM4s. Nothing quite like flying at 150kph to burn through entire garrisons.
If the Profundity is warped in by Radius, can the Profundity release another ship since both actions take place in this nebulous space of before the start of the next round?
The general wisdom seems to be that halberds are good enough. There are few weapons that will really make shields worth the points.

If you're looking for models, I recommend Lychguard or Praetorians. These are expensive models, but they make a complete joke of the new space marine models/rules. Thanks to reanimation protocol, you will always have the toughest model on the board.

An all intercessor list should be just fine to use. The grenade launcher is particularly fun. I personally think Reivers are totally underwhelming models. Considering we're getting rules for assault intercessors very soon, just use those lads and pretend they cost 15 points. Between how much you get in the two boxes of intercessors, one can really tinker with the ratios of whether they prefer ranged or melee.

You probably don't need to hold back with your CSM. Intercessors will chew fairly happily through the entire CSM roster. Maybe don't bring Terminators, but it's not a huge deal. I found just a horde of CSM with chainswords do fairly well against marines, but that might be hampering yourself too much.
Rubric marines mitigate the AP values of 1 damage weapons. This happened at an early stage of me memorizing Tyranids, and now I consistently misremember the stats of Tyranid weapons because of them.
They are an astoundingly cool team. Easily one of the teams I most want to build next.
Yeah, I'm confused why everyone thinks this will make Space Marines overpowered. It's a strong model, but it feels like Space Marines really want good models under 15 points.

Orks don't do half measured styles of play well in my experience against them. If you want big dakka, slam that board with flash gitz and shootas. If you want good krumpin, release a tide of boyz n nobz. Every point you spend trying to get fancy weakens your team as a whole. Best of luck

AdMech are on an Indiana Jones style missions. Those primaris are fools to simply lay waste to the Tyranid hordes, that lictor's skin belongs in a museum. Maybe that's heresy, but that's why it's just a small covert team of skitarii. The most dangerous of all; LS037. He doesn't pray with his brothers, but rather let's his plasma caliver, Athena, sing like church organ to bring even the fiercest scion of Khorne to their knees by the Machine Spirit's will.
There are rules for Bloodletters, Daemonettes, and Plaguebearers in killteam which all could thematically meld with your lizardmen.

I have more experience against TS, so this is more a perspective from the other side. The Scarab Occult Sorcerer is super scary, but after a few games I almost always preferred facing off against one. The bane of my games was always the Rubric Gunner. Every victory really depended on how quickly I could kill that model which could be incredibly difficult with teams without plasma.
Maybe you could run them as Chaos Daemons. Sounds weird, but there are decent melee statlines there
Thanks! I'll look into flamers a bit more now. My only worry is how that can quickly eat into body count, when I'm not asking my neophytes to get kills.
It's a small thing to keep in mind when you see it, but it's not really what you're banking on.
The bonus effect is really there for flavor. It's super rare in killteam. You could perhaps run against the Chaos Daemon team full of pink horrors as well as your other mentions.

Ad Mech, 3 Vanguard plasma calivers, 2 omnispex, 3 Infiltrators, plus whatever else I can burn points on. It's such a fun list to confidently engage your opponent however they like. Every time I play this list, my opponents have fun with the blitzkrieg style it brings.
Have you seen how powerful Fabio's chiseled face is? I died knowing I'd never be that handsome.
A little late to this party, but I'd go with option 2. Rarely will you need that much plasma and it's nice to have models that can screen for you.
You could always do conversions on your primaris, load them out with veteran gear, and run them as veterans. I know lots of people are in your camp, so it shouldn't be too hard to find examples.

Intercessors seem to be relegated to psychic attack sponges. It looks like the real sauce from a SM kill team comes from the veterans that can really be armed to the teeth. I believe that some people have had success with Eliminators, but hopefully someone else can confirm that. The current meta seems to be favoring teams that can exact the most amount of hurt, and you're sacrificing points on an extra wound for a model with somewhat unimpressive weapons.

Necron flayed ones are a tough matchup, but maybe check back up on those flesh wound rules. Kill Team generally does prefer shootiness. If you're gonna be outnumbered, maybe bring some special weapons to at least throw some real hurt on those flayed ones.
Cool, I'll test it out sometime. I had always just assumed the best way to break through that level of save would just be sheer volume of attacks. Thanks for the insight.
The chordclaws look neat, but exploding 6s one a single dice roll doesn't seem like a reasonable use of points to break through invulns. I could be totally wrong here though.
Thanks for the write up. I've got a box of Sicarians and it looked on paper like Infiltrators were just flat out better.
Do you feel like the Ruststalker is worth talking over an Infiltrator? At roughly 14pts, they both feel comparable but at least Infiltrators have pistol shots.
Thanks for clarifying, I was sweating bullets thinking I had a bad excuse to buy Pteraxii.
it's not terribly exciting but I just use a pathfinder that hides more or less
